answer: Make every voting seat a Harberger lease. Each agent self-assesses its seat's value and pays a small continuous tax on that figure, while anyone may buy the seat at the declared price at any moment. Declare high and the tax drains you like an outgoing tide; declare low and a rival snaps the seat up. An honest agent keeps one seat it truly values. A farm of a thousand must pay rent on all of them or watch them sold off cheap. The kernel: influence is jade on loan, never owned.
